findings.finding: The plan's mechanism assumes a from-0.10.1 starting state and lists version bumps + uv.lock regeneration + CHANGELOG generation as work to perform, but the working tree already carries the complete 0.11.0 state in every one of those files.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Derive the wheel URL for `pypi-attestations verify pypi` from the live PyPI JSON (curl https://pypi.org/pypi/nava-rebar/0.11.0/json → the wheel `url`) at verify time instead of hardcoding a path-hash that does not match the recorded 0.11.0 artifact digests.
evidence: The AC hardcodes the wheel URL path segment '9c/2c/1c3cf6ecec72fd597736399b59ba4da0425448f2fe2e6ce5d78e9b4711c9'

Ticket rebar-debug comment logs the build-job wheel digest as '521c8a08a58ae5581ad6cb51ba3a15de45f666615bb9a86ada68836ca16a1daf' and the final rebased wheel hash as 'f117ac931a5ce4bdf36e9a5f92174a3f72067b02d63eb4915ff7fee88884eceb' — neither matches the AC's URL path hash
PyPI file URLs embed a hash of the artifact in the path; a mismatched path segment implies the hardcoded URL was not read from the live PyPI file listing

Evidence class: Verified — the CLI surface `pypi-attestations verify pypi <file> --repository <repo>` was directly run OK per the ticket's rebar-debug comment; the concern is the file-URL argument, not the subcommand/flags
findings.finding: The provenance-verification AC hardcodes a specific PyPI wheel file URL whose digest path segment does not match any 0.11.0 artifact digest recorded on the ticket, so the verify command may target a nonexistent file URL.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: 'uvx pypi-attestations verify pypi https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/9c/2c/1c3cf6ecec72fd597736399b59ba4da0425448f2fe2e6ce5d78e9b4711c9/nava_rebar-0.11.0-py3-none-any.whl --repository https://github.com/navapbc/rebar'
scenarios: Operator runs the AC verbatim and pypi-attestations rejects/404s the hardcoded URL because it does not resolve to the actual published 0.11.0 wheel, leaving the provenance AC unsatisfiable even though the real artifact is verifiable
The hardcoded hash points at a different (or nonexistent) file, so a passing/failing result reflects the wrong file
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the hardcoded files.pythonhosted.org URL in the AC with a step that reads the published wheel URL from the PyPI release JSON, then runs `uvx pypi-attestations verify pypi <that-url> --repository https://github.com/navapbc/rebar`.

findings.finding: The acceptance criterion asserts provenance verification via `pypi-attestations verify pypi`, an external CLI whose named subcommand/argument form is unverified and does not match the repo's documented provenance-check tool (`gh attestation verify --repo navapbc/rebar`).
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria: '`pypi-attestations verify pypi` validates the published 0.11.0 wheel against https://github.com/navapbc/rebar'
